Each transition reduced size and power while increasing reliability and speed. The stored-program architecture, in which instructions and data share one memory, remains the organizing idea behind nearly every general-purpose machine built since. Memory hierarchies developed because fast storage is expensive and dense storage is slow, so designers interpose caches between processors and main memory.
